lines.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W with header
lines.notes: Lives in the head. The only orderable offer on 2026-10-13 is Seeed Studio's Basic Kit 114060102 (board with pre-soldered header plus 'basic essential accessories' that Seeed does not list), shipped from China under DAP terms, so US duty is extra and not in the quote. PiShop 112-1 ($20.75) shows no stock text at all, while PiShop's in-stock pages say 'IN STOCK', so it is treated as sold out (ask PiShop before ordering). Adafruit, SparkFun, CanaKit (board only), Pimoroni and Mouser (backorder to 2027-01-25) are out of stock. Lock in supply before anything else. One spare.

lines.name: microSD card, 32 GB, Class 10

spec.class: Class 10 or better (A1/A2 not required on a Zero 2 W)

lines.mpn: SanDisk 32 GB Class 10 with Raspberry Pi OS (PiShop 1363-1)
alternates: Raspberry Pi SC1628 32 GB A2 (PiShop 907-1, stock not shown)
Raspberry Pi SC2121Q 64 GB A2 (Mouser, in stock, $35.25)
lines.notes: Spec relaxed from A2: the A2 speed-up needs command queueing, which only the Pi 5 host uses, so a Class 10 card performs the same on a Zero 2 W. The official A2 card (SC1628) is out of stock or restricted at Adafruit, SparkFun and Mouser, and PiShop 907-1 shows no stock, so the in-stock SanDisk card at the same $19.95 is pinned. Its page gives no A1/A2 rating. The pre-loaded OS is replaced when the card is flashed.

lines.mpn: Adafruit 3446 (Pi Foundation Raspberry Pi Zero Case + Mini Camera Cable)
alternates: Adafruit 3157 (150 mm, too long for the head)
Raspberry Pi SC1128 (200 mm, too long)
lines.notes: The path in the head is about 32 mm (Pi camera connector to the camera's FPC edge), so a 200 mm cable would leave 170 mm to stow in a 20 mm gap. The 38 mm cable from the official Zero case kit is the shortest Standard-Mini cable on a fetched page; the case itself goes unused. Test-fit it on the first unit. Two spares.

lines.name: Adafruit Perma Proto Bonnet Mini Kit
lines.notes: Carries all head wiring instead of a custom PCB. Stock is thin: Mouser had 21 on 2026-10-13 and 21 are bought (one spare), so recheck right before ordering; Adafruit has 5. Check on the first kit that the 2x20 header is a female socket.

lines.name: Adafruit I2S 3 W Class D Amplifier Breakout, MAX98357A

spec.outputW: 3.2 W into 4 ohm at 5 V, 10% THD

lines.notes: SD_MODE is driven from GPIO16 at 3.3 V, which selects the left channel (MAX98357A datasheet Table 5), not the breakout's (L+R)/2 default, so the client plays mono. Volume capped at 2.5 W in software (asound.conf softvol).

lines.name: Speaker, 40 mm, 4 ohm, 3 W
alternates: Adafruit 3968 (40 mm 4 ohm; Jameco 2516055, 2-week lead; Adafruit out of stock)
lines.notes: PUI Audio. Lives in the base under a grille. Pinned to Master Electronics, the only in-stock source of this part (315, minimum 20, multiples of 20). The cheaper-looking Jameco row is a different speaker (Adafruit 3968: 20 mm tall, 27.3 g, stock not shown, 2-week lead, non-returnable), so it is kept only as an alternate. DigiKey shows 0 with an 18-week lead. Height 18.3 mm is on the PUI product page; the spec sheet gives a 35.6 mm baffle opening, which the grille now matches.

lines.name: Miniature DPDT toggle, on-on, solder lugs, 1/4-40 bushing

spec.retention: fixed (lever is part of the switch, panel nut)

alternates: Adafruit 3220 (6 mm bushing, out of stock)
lines.notes: Substitute for Adafruit 3220, which is out of stock. Same DPDT ON-ON function with solder lugs, but a 1/4-40 bushing: the head's toggle hole is 6.5 mm (was 6 mm) and the CAD envelope for the body is 13.2 x 13.2 mm (was 13.1 x 12.6). Jameco's page gives two sets of sizes (0.52 x 0.52 x 0.38 in in the features, 0.5 x 0.45 x 0.35 in in the table); the larger is used. Check the first switch against the head before printing 20. Jameco gives a 5 A at 125 VAC rating and no contact material; power-rated silver contacts switching about 1 mA and 3 MHz I2S data can go intermittent over months, so a gold-contact DPDT is better for the next build (none fetched yet). Test mute on every unit. Pinned to Jameco so both orders get the same switch (the Mouser E-Switch alternate is cheaper for 2 but is a different body). Jameco adds a $5 processing fee to orders under $10, which order A (2 toggles, $4.50) is: buy 6 there, or accept the fee.

lines.notes: Two per unit: 690 mm of one becomes the arm harness, the rest of both is peeled into single wires for the head and base jumpers (about 3.5 m needed per unit). Adafruit page: 220 ohm/km, 1.2 mm wire OD, 22 g. One spare.

lines.name: 15 in flexible 1/8 IPS gooseneck, matte black

spec.thread: 1/8 IPS; the page's keywords say male, the gender at each end is not stated
spec.hollow: not stated on the page (sold as lamp pipe)

lines.mpn: Grand Brass 15in. Flexible 1/8ips Goose Neck Pipe - Matte Black (image code PIGN15BL)
alternates: Grand Brass 12in matte black (PIGN12BL, $24.32): too short for the 165 deg turn into the head's top coupling
lines.notes: Lamp gooseneck. The head hangs from its end through the head's top face, so the arm leaves the base pointing up and turns about 165 deg to enter the head: at a 40 mm bend radius that needs about 335 mm, which the 12 in (305 mm) can't give. Hollow, thread gender, bore and weight are not on the page: buy two for the first-article build and check them before ordering the rest.
